lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: interpreting model parameters in context

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A population of 1800 grows by 3% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 6 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 94 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 2, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
A stays ahead permanently because 94 is larger than 2.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 3600(0.95)^t, with t in years. What does 0.95 represent?
choices: the value of the asset when it was new, $3600
the total value lost over the asset's life
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.95, meaning a 5% annual loss

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (2, 21) and (6, 57). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 8, 11, 14, 17. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 3.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 3.

items.prompt: A population of 400 grows by 16% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 2 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 86 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 2, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
A stays ahead permanently because 86 is larger than 2.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 3900(0.92)^t, with t in years. What does 0.92 represent?
choices: the fraction of value retained each year, 0.92, meaning a 8% annual loss
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the value of the asset when it was new, $3900
the total value lost over the asset's life

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (4, -3) and (8, 1). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 13, 39, 117, 351. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 3.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 3.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
